title: Minimum Household Income Required to Employ Migrant Domestic Worker
what_it_is: Minimum Household Income Required to Employ Migrant Domestic Worker

sections.label: MDW eligibility assessment factors
sections.summary: MOM assesses MDW eligibility using employer income, accommodation ability and household caregiving needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: MOM assesses an applicant's eligibility to employ a migrant domestic worker (MDW) based on various factors, such as the income of the prospective employer, the ability to provide proper and safe accommodation for the domestic worker and the caregiving needs of the household.

sections.label: MDW renewal application assessments
sections.summary: Renewals consider employer track records like salary or levy defaults; about 2,000 cases, or 1%, were rejected yearly over five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In assessing renewal applications, we also consider the track records of the employers, such as whether they previously defaulted on salary or levy payment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Hence, we do not have a rigid income criterion and do not just reject applications solely on that alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Over the past five years, an average of about 2,000 cases, or about 1% of all the applications each year, were rejected after taking the various factors into consideration.

sections.label: Financial ability and applicant discussion
sections.summary: MOM considers various forms of financial ability and has been in discussion with the referred resident's applicant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Indeed, we do consider various forms of financial ability for the applicant to be able to hire an MDW.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And in the case of the resident who was referred to MOM, we have actually been in discussion with the applicant.
